attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
EVENT MEDICAL PLAN
Lakeshore Community Run 10K, Sunday 4 April 2027
Applicant: Lakeshore Striders
Issue: 2.0

1. Event summary
A 10K race with 150 runners, starting at 09:00 in the Tanners Row area of Port Halden. An ambulance from Sentinel Ambulance Service is on site for the race; the paperwork is attached.

2. First aid cover
3 first aid posts will operate, at the start, at the finish and at the course midpoint, staffed by 12 qualified first aiders. Posts are placed so that no part of the course is more than 1.5 km from one. Two cycle responders move along the course with defibrillators.

Some background. Our committee has run this race for a number of years and takes the welfare of runners to heart. One of our longtime members is a retired paramedic who usually runs the race herself and is not on duty that day.

3. Weather and hydration
Water is available every 2.5 km. The race director checks the forecast 48 hours and 2 hours before the start. Above 28 degrees C the start is brought forward or the course shortened, and above 32 degrees C the race is cancelled. In cold or wet conditions, foil blankets and a warm shelter are at the finish.

4. Transfer to hospital
The receiving hospital is Port Halden General Hospital, 10 km from the finish. The transfer route and the pick-up point at the top of Hatter Street have been walked with the first aid team. The hospital's emergency department has been told the date and the expected numbers.

5. Communications
Every first aid post and cycle responder carries a radio on the medical channel, with phones as backup. All calls for an ambulance go through the medical lead, who gives the crew the access point and the nearest barrier to open.

6. Clinical lead
The medical lead is Ines Moreau, a registered paramedic, who is on site from an hour before the start until the last runner is cleared. The lead can have any runner withdrawn on medical grounds.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
RACE PLAN
Lakeshore Community Run 10K | Sunday 4 April 2027
Organiser: Lakeshore Striders
Race director: Ellis Grant
Reference: PH-57295

Overview
The Lakeshore Community Run 10K is a 10K race of 10 km for 150 entrants, based in the Tanners Row area of Port Halden. The start is at 09:00 and the course closes at 11:00.

Course
The course runs in order along Hatter Street, Halden Way, Mill Road, Castle Way, Brook Street and Tanner Street, all of which are closed to traffic for the race. Major roads crossed: Canal Road, High Street, Church Road, Regent Road and Queen's Road. The finish is in Exchange Square.

Course dimensions
Survey widths: Hatter Street 9 m, Castle Way 14 m, Tanner Street 9 m, kerb to kerb, excluding footways. Start pens sit side by side across the full carriageway, and spectators have the pavement and a grassed verge along most of the route.

Support
Entrants collect numbers from the top of Hatter Street from one hour before the start. Timing is by chip, with mats at the start and finish. Results are posted on the Lakeshore website the same day.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN
Event: Lakeshore Community Run 10K
Date: Sunday 4 April 2027
Applicant: Lakeshore Striders
Prepared by: Brightway Traffic Consulting
Issue: 2.0

1. Scope
This plan describes how traffic will be managed for the Lakeshore Community Run 10K, a 10K race in the Tanners Row area of Port Halden with a 09:00 start. It has been prepared to accompany the permit application and should be read with the race plan. See the attached correspondence from the police for the escort.

2. Road closures
Temporary closures will be in force as follows, with barriers and advance signing supplied by Northline Barriers.
- Hatter Street, Copper Row to Bell Street: closed 08:00 to 11:30
- Halden Way, Ash Avenue to Dyer Street: closed 08:00 to 11:30
- Mill Road, Fenwick Street to Ash Avenue: closed 08:00 to 11:30
- Castle Way, Copper Row to Dyer Street: closed 08:00 to 11:30
- Brook Street, Ash Avenue to Bridge Row: closed 08:00 to 11:30
- Tanner Street, Dyer Street to Copper Row: closed 08:00 to 11:30

3. Major crossings
Each major crossing has its own control point, staffed from 08:00 until the last runner has passed.
- Canal Road at Halden Way: 2 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor
- High Street at Halden Way: 3 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor
- Church Road at Hatter Street: 3 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor
- Regent Road at Halden Way: 2 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor
- Queen's Road at Brook Street: 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor

4. Diversions
Signed diversions will operate for the duration of the closures.
- Hatter Street: traffic diverted via Victoria Road and Tram Street, signed from Bridge Row
- Halden Way: traffic diverted via Station Road and Tram Street, signed from Bell Street
- Mill Road: traffic diverted via Prince Street and Victoria Road, signed from Fenwick Street
- Castle Way: traffic diverted via Victoria Road and Cross Avenue, signed from Dyer Street
- Brook Street: traffic diverted via Prince Street and Victoria Road, signed from Dyer Street
- Tanner Street: traffic diverted via Prince Street and Station Road, signed from Copper Row

5. Emergency vehicle access
A clear lane of at least 3.5 m will be kept along the closed section for emergency vehicles. Barrier staff hold radios on the event channel and can open any closure within two minutes on request from the event controller, who is in direct contact with the police and ambulance control rooms.

The route has changed little from last time. Where it has changed, we have tried to keep a clear run for the field, and we welcome any comments from the Events Office on how signed diversions are usually handled in the city.

6. Notification
Details of the event will be published on the organiser's website and shared through social media in the weeks leading up to race day.

7. Reopening
A sweep vehicle follows the last runner. Closures are lifted in the order listed, after a barrier and litter check, with all roads open by 11:30.
